nytimes_articles.abstract: William N Wallace in Notebook column notes that Syracuse quarterback Donovan McNabb ran for 162 yards in 52-21 victory over Virginia Tech and Army quarterback Ron McAda will miss game against Yale because of injured left ankle (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: BUSINESS DIGEST
Hazards Fixed, New Technical School Is Set to Open
nytimes_articles.abstract: Classes at High School for Cooperative Technical Education are scheduled to begin on Oct 2, more than two weeks after Manhattan school's opening was delayed by Board of Education because of building violations it deemed dangerous to teachers and students (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Electronics Slump in Asia May Soon Be Over
nytimes_articles.abstract: Evidence is emerging that the slowdown in the global electronics industry, which has crimped East Asia's economic growth and exports in 1996, is temporary and that a recovery will occur in 1997, analysts say..That is good news for countries like Singap

nytimes_articles.headline: Kiwi Declares Bankruptcy and Trims Routes
nytimes_articles.abstract: Kiwi International Air Lines, low-cost carrier started by former pilots of Eastern Airlines in 1992, files for bankruptcy protection; says it will shrink its route structure to serve three cities--Newark, Atlanta and Chicago, and drop service to Tampa and Orlando, Las Vegas and Bermuda; Kiwi has been plagued with problems since its inception; Jerry Murphy, Kiwi's chief executive, says debt accumulated in its first three years of business proved insurmountable, even though airline posted three recent consecutive quarters of profit (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Look at Tuition Costs As Shackles From Jail
nytimes_articles.abstract: Letter from Jess Bravin, regent, University of California, comments on rise in college tuition at public universities

nytimes_articles.headline: What Russian Crisis?
nytimes_articles.abstract: Michael McFaul Op-Ed article on issue of presidential succession in Russia; holds no matter the outcome of Boris Yeltsin's coming heart surgery, uncertainty about his ability to serve out his second term has jump-started planning and plotting to succeed him; describes how Russia's political landscape has changed since July presidential election (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Giuliani Leading Democratic Rivals, Marist Poll Reports
nytimes_articles.abstract: Marist Institute for Public Opinion poll finds that 13 months before he can seek re-election, Mayor Rudolph W Giuliani is leading potential Democratic rivals, but he remains polarizing figure, with white residents far more pleased with his performance than Hispanic and black ones (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Patterns
nytimes_articles.abstract: Calvin Klein, Ralph Lauren and Donna Karan will not show their signature collections at Bryant Park ready-to-wear shows; Diego Della Valle is converting his signature stores to J P Tod's boutiques; BCBG Max Azria, Los Angeles apparel company, has expanded this year (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Jury Orders Tyson to Pay His Former Trainer More Than $4.4 Million
nytimes_articles.abstract: Federal jury orders heavyweight champion Mike Tyson to pay his former trainer Kevin Rooney more than $4.4 million to settle lawsuit brought by Rooney, who says Tyson had broken lifetime contract for Rooney to train fighter (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Birger Lunde, Norway Seaman; Survivor of Nazi U-Boats Was 82
nytimes_articles.abstract: Birger Lunde, who served in Norwegian merchant marine during World War II and was awarded medal for bravery by King Haakon VII, dies at age 82 (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Is Medical Rivalry Threatening Yeltsin's Chances for Recovery?
nytimes_articles.abstract: Lawrence K Altman comments on Boris Yeltsin's insistence on having delicate heart bypass operation done in Moscow, apparently because of national pride and precarious hold on power; notes suggestion that this could make him vulnerable to 'the VIP syndrome,' jeopardizing chances of successful outcome; photos of Dr Michael E DeBakey, and Dr Renat S Akchurin, Russian surgeon who is operate on Yeltsin (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: On Drugs, Bruises and Betrayal
nytimes_articles.abstract: Jon Pareles reviews new CD's from Scrawl, Lisa Germano, The Cardigans, The Wedding Present and Donna Lewis; (Critic's Choice column) (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Corrections
Mental Health Contracts Questioned in Audit
nytimes_articles.abstract: New York City Comptroller Alan G Hevesi audit raises new questions about how Giuliani administration awards millions of dollars in contracts, contending that mental health officials have repeatedly ignored guidelines that are intended to prevent mismanagement and patronage; finds that in many instances, Department of Mental Health, Mental Retardation and Alcoholism Services had no documentation to explain why it awarded 30 contracts worth $8.4 million in fiscal 1995 (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Umpires Vote To Boycott Over Alomar
nytimes_articles.abstract: Major League Baseball umpires vote not to work playoffs unless American League pres Gene Budig suspends Roberto Alomar of Baltimore Orioles for first round of playoffs for spitting in face of Umpire John Hirschbeck during dispute over called third strike (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Mellow Boss Lets Bats Do the Talking
nytimes_articles.abstract: George Steinbrenner 3d, principal owner of New York Yankees, who have won their first American League Eastern Division championship in 15 years, is famous for hiring and firing managers and losing his temper in public; this season he has steered clear of limelight; in stark contrast to previous years, Steinbrenner has largely let his current manager, Joe Torre, and general manager, Bob Watson, do talking for ball club that even some of his sternest critics give him credit for assembling; his close friend Bill Fugazy says Steinbrenner seems to have been chastened by deaths of Billy Martin in 1989 and Mickey Mantle last year; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: In London Shows, Individuality Stands Out
nytimes_articles.abstract: Amy M Spindler reviews spring fashion shows presented during London fashion week; photos (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Democratic Tide Is Eroding G.O.P.'s Stronghold in West
nytimes_articles.abstract: Article in series The Race for President discusses erosion of Republican strength in West; George Bush fared poorly in region in 1992, and Bob Dole is struggling to head off debacle, especially in California; 13 Western states, mostly conservative stronghold until l992, are poised to become solid part of Democratic base in years to come; only sparsely populated Alaska, Wyoming, Idaho and Utah seem firmly committed to Dole, but these states have only 15 electoral votes compared with 54 in California alone; Clinton has comfortable lead most everywhere else, even in Arizona, which last voted for Democratic president in 1948; Ross Perot ran strongly in region in 1992, but shows hardly any strength this year (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Corrections
Wetteland Honored as A.L.'s Top Reliever
nytimes_articles.abstract: John Wetteland of New York Yankees and Jeff Brantley of Cincinnati Reds win Rolaids relief awards for being top closers in American and National Leagues (S)

nytimes_articles.abstract: Sports transactions

nytimes_articles.headline: Merger to Create Biggest Maker of Air Bags
nytimes_articles.abstract: Autoliv AB, Swedish car-safety group, announces plans to create world's largest air-bag manufacturer through its merger with ASP, auto-safety division of Morton International of Chicago; new company, to be known as Autoliv Inc, will have annual revenue of $3 billion and 15,000 employees; head office will be in Europe, but legal domicile will be in United States; deal is portrayed as 'merger of equals' under which Autoliv AB's owners will exchange their interest for 53.5 percent of shares in new company, and owners of Morton International will swap ASP for 46.5 percent of shares in new company (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: 3 Bickering Bosnian Leaders Finally Begin to Plan a Nation
nytimes_articles.abstract: Bosnia's new Government takes first small step as three men holding joint presidency hold meeting in hotel at edge of Sarajevo; UN envoy Carl Bildt reports Serb Momcilo Krajisnik, Croat Kresimir Zubak and Muslim Alija Izetbegovic agreed to timetable for convening national legislature and appointing council of ministers, and also setting up telephone lines (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Fish-Farm Escapees Threaten Wild Salmon
nytimes_articles.abstract: Wild Atlantic salmon returning to spawn in freshwater streams of their birth now face startling threat: interlopers; new research shows that more than quarter of spawning salmon in Norwegian rivers and streams are escapees from fish farms--fish hatched in metal tanks, vaccinated against infections and raised in sea pens artificially lighted to speed maturation; geneticists warn that without stiffer controls, rapidly growing aquaculture industry in Europe and North America could wipe out what is left of wild Atlantic salmon population; photos (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Executive Changes
nytimes_articles.abstract: Chevron Corp says Ray Galvin would retire as corporate vice president and president of Chevron USA Production Co; says Peter Robertson will replace him, and Greg Matiuk will succeed Robertson as corporate vice president (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: State Jobs, but Not on Paper
nytimes_articles.abstract: As one of economy measures in Gov Christine Todd Whitman's current budget, state has stopped publishing list of vacant Civil Service jobs (New Jersey Daily Briefing) (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: I.B.M. TO ACQUIRE AN INSURANCE SOFTWARE COMPANY
nytimes_articles.abstract: International Business Machines Corp agrees to acquire Professional Data Management Associates Inc; terms are not disclosed (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Ground Tests Loom for Ultimate Hot Rods, Supersonic Cars
nytimes_articles.abstract: Competing teams of highly innovative car designers are about to go after last major speed hurdle on land: breaking the sound barrier by hurtling across dry lake at dizzying speeds of 760 miles an hour or more; with vehicles just off the ground, buffeted by forces that no one can foretell with certainty, risks are as staggering as potential glory; several groups around world have built or are designing and building jet-powered cars that they say will break land speed record of 633.47 miles an hour; two major players in challenge are Craig Breedlove and Richard Noble; photos; drawings (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Prices Lower On Treasury Securities
nytimes_articles.abstract: Prices of Treasury securities turn lower for second consecutive session, mostly on strength of housing report that surprised market and raised investors' concerns about inflation and higher interest rates; 30-year bond slips 3/32, to 97 28/32; graph (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Politics Aside, Economy Is Shrugging Off Rise to $4.75
nytimes_articles.abstract: Increase in minimum wage to $4.75 an hour will affect only 3.3 percent of all workers, and impact on overall economy will be negligible; many economists predict small job losses--200,000 at most over two years in a work force of 126 million; economists agree that inflationary jolt will amount to one-tenth or two-tenths of 1 percent this year, because so few earn the minimum wage; Barry P Bosworth, economist at Brookings Institution, says even second increase, to $5.15 next September, will mean raises for 5.4 million additional workers, but will not change equation much; even in Detroit, Mich, where unemployment is nearly twice the national rate, much of the economy has moved beyond minimum-wage levels; Labor Sec Robert B Reich bristles at notion that higher minimum wage would not make much diference to workers making lowest wages; photo; graphs (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Jazz Giant Roving Around the Piano Keys
nytimes_articles.abstract: Profile of jazz pianist Oscar Peterson, who is being honored with tribute at Town Hall, filled with friends and band members past and present; photo (M)
